title: Perception gap video: replication, mechanism and persistence
why: Addresses power and design: it gives the one borderline effect a large pre-registered replication, adds a mechanism measure, and adds a delayed follow-up.

power_target.basis: Observed −2.3 points with SE 0.997 at n=641; the true effect is probably smaller than the winning estimate, so size for about 1.4 points (SD about 20 implied by the SEs).

rationale: In the source study the Perception gap video lowered the thermometer gap by 2.3 points (SE 0.997, n=641, p=0.021), one borderline result among 64 uncorrected tests. This follow-up replicates it at scale, tests whether correcting out-party misperceptions is the channel by comparing the full video with a version lacking the misperception data, and re-measures after about 2 weeks because the source only measured outcomes immediately.
contribution: Separates a replicated effect of the perception gap video from placebo and attention effects, tests whether the misperception correction carries it, and shows whether it persists.
hypothesis: The full Perception gap video lowers the in-party minus out-party thermometer gap relative to control by about 1.4 points or more. The effect is mediated by reduced misperception of out-party attitudes, so the no-data variant has a smaller effect. Some of the effect remains at about 2 weeks. Undemocratic-practice support does not increase.
primary_outcome: Affective polarization (in-party minus out-party thermometer) immediately after exposure, full video versus control.
comparison: Primary test: full Perception gap video versus control. Secondary: full video versus no-data variant (the correction), full video versus placebo, mediation by change in perceived out-party attitudes, wave 2 persistence, and support for undemocratic practices.
unresolved: Video files and the edited no-data version must be produced by the research team.

title: Who does the Perception gap video work for?
why: Addresses sample and measurement: the exploratory interactions were too noisy (CIs of ±7 points), so a dedicated, powered moderator test is needed.

power_target.basis: E2/E3 interaction SEs of 3-3.6 at the arm sizes used; the interaction MDE needs about 4x the n of the main effect.

rationale: The Perception gap video lowered affective polarization by 2.3 points (95% CI [-4.3, -0.4], n=641 vs control 229), but exploratory party and interest interactions were null with intervals of about ±7 points. A dedicated, stratified, powered test is needed to learn whether the effect depends on partisanship, political interest or baseline misperception.
contribution: Provides a preregistered, powered test of three moderators of the Perception gap video effect on affective polarization.
hypothesis: The video effect on affective polarization is larger (more negative) for respondents with larger baseline misperception; effects of party and interest are tested as two-sided preregistered interactions.
primary_outcome: Affective polarization: in-party minus out-party feeling thermometer after treatment.
comparison: Video vs control, with treatment x party, treatment x political interest and treatment x baseline misperception interactions, adjusted for pre-treatment polarization.
unresolved: The actual Perception gap video file must be supplied and hosted by the research team.
IRB approval number and compensation details must be supplied by the research team.
The panel vendor and quota feasibility for 2400 respondents must be confirmed.

title: Individual message versus structural cue
why: Addresses framing: it tests whether individual-level correction is overridden by structural cues, instead of assuming either side.

power_target.basis: Interaction contrast; the observed main effect of −2.3 with SE 1.0 at n=641 implies an interaction needs roughly 800 per cell.

rationale: Only the Perception gap video lowered affective polarization (-2.3, 95% CI [-4.3, -0.4], n=641) among 32 arms, and the study cannot test structural causes. This 2x2 crosses the video with a hostile elite/media feed prime to see whether the individual-level correction survives a hostile environment.
contribution: Directly tests whether an individual-level perception correction is overridden by structural hostility cues rather than assuming either account.
hypothesis: If individual interventions have leverage, the video lowers affective polarization under both primes. If the structural account holds, the video effect shrinks or vanishes under the hostile prime (video x prime interaction > 0).
primary_outcome: Affective polarization: in-party minus out-party feeling thermometer.
comparison: Video vs control within each prime; the video x prime interaction contrast; secondary outcome is support for undemocratic practices.
unresolved: Actual feed screenshots and the Perception gap video file must be supplied by the research team.
IRB approval number and compensation must be supplied.
